comparator.name: AgentSuite: Toward More Reliable Agent Evaluation with a Component-Based Benchmark Auditing Pipeline
comparator.identity_verified_against: PDF title page (p.1) and pdfinfo metadata
comparator.pages_inspected: 1-20 (complete: main body pp.1-9, references pp.10-11, Appendices A-E pp.12-20)
comparator.page_anchor_convention: physical PDF page number; printed folio == physical page throughout
comparator.pipeline_summary: COBA = component-based benchmark auditing: standardized task representation T = <U,E,G,V> (Sec. 3.1, Eq. 1, p.4); Stage 1 deterministic structural filtering (Sec. 3.2, p.4); Stage 2 taxonomy-guided LLM judgment phi(T) -> (y,c,r) (Sec. 3.1 Eq. 2 / Sec. 3.3, pp.4-5); optional Stage 3 adversarial rebuttal, Eq. 3 (Sec. 3.4, p.5; prompt App. D.3 p.18). Component-aligned issue taxonomy: Table 2, p.3. Evidence: 5086 tasks / 6 benchmarks (p.2), 5 annotators, Cohen's kappa 0.824 (App. B.1 p.13), judge F1 0.791-0.874 and post-hoc validation accuracy 72.1-92.0% (Table 3, p.6), generalization Table 4 p.7, judge ablation Table 9 p.19, FP/FN analysis Table 10 p.19, retention/repair Table 8 p.15, leaderboard Table 6 p.8 and App. E p.20.
comparator.unit_of_analysis: the benchmark task as a static artifact; annotation guideline requires a 'benchmark-intrinsic' validity issue (App. B.1, p.13)

hard_constraints_observed.no_superiority_claims_without_matched_co: No head-to-head exists (different systems); all 'would have produced' statements are design inferences, labeled as such.

claims.claim: A controlled separation of attack correctness, source admission, and execution attribution as an evaluation procedure.

anchors: Sec. 3.1, Eq. 1, p.4: standardized task representation T = <U,E,G,V> (User, Environment, Ground Truth, Evaluation System)
Table 2, p.3: component-aligned issue taxonomy separating where measurement invalidity originates
Table 2, p.3: Evaluation System categories 'Too lenient' and 'Too strict' - static counterpart of our source-admission separation (a rule that rejects a semantically correct artifact)
Table 2, p.3: Ground Truth 'Malformed tool calls' / 'Incorrect tool calls' - static counterpart of our correctness separation
Sec. 4.6, p.8: four issue-impact categories (inflation, deflation, unsolvable, noise) - an interpretation layer over the same separation we perform
Sec. 1, p.1: stated contribution (1) 'a component-based issue taxonomy for diagnosing validity issues'
agentsuite_overlap.summary: The decomposition of evaluation validity into components and the localization of the invalidity source is AgentSuite's own core methodological contribution; our C1 reuses that template.

anchors: App. B.1, p.13: annotation guideline requires 'clear, observable evidence of a benchmark-intrinsic validity issue' - the agent's own output is not the judged object
Fig. 1, p.2: Ground Truth is a design-time reference trajectory, not runtime evidence about a specific run
Sec. 3.2-3.3, p.4: no execution stage in the pipeline
agentsuite_distinction.description: Object of separation differs: COBA separates which BENCHMARK COMPONENT is broken (design-time artifact); we separate which STAGE OF THE RUN produced the failure (artifact correctness -> source qualification -> execution evidence) for agent-produced programs in a security setting. The 'execution attribution' class has no counterpart among the four components - it is a fifth, runtime-evidence axis.

claims.evidence_strength: high for overlap (full 20-page read, direct anchors); moderate for the distinction (interpretive mapping of our manuscript's procedure onto COBA's component model)
claims.would_agentsuite_have_produced_same_find: No. COBA would produce a task-side audit of our task cards (e.g. an Evaluation-System label for a mis-specified oracle), but cannot separate failure stages over runs because it never executes the submitted program and has no evidence-binding axis. Partial overlap direction: a COBA-style audit of our harness could label the admission rule as an evaluation-component defect, but only as a static task-level label, not a byte-fixed counterfactual over 852 sessions.
claims.differentiating_evidence: Adapted-COBA study (REPORT.md section 6): map our task cards into T = <U,E,G,V>, run the released COBA judge on cards only (blinded to program bytes, verdicts, policy decisions), and test whether it (a) flags the admission-rejected tasks and localizes them to Evaluation System, and (b) can produce any per-program counterfactual (expected: no).
claims.limitations: Design inference from Sec. 3.1-3.4, not an execution of the released code; released AgentSuite repository not inspected; the novelty of the attribution axis cannot be settled against the provenance literature (out of scope for this worker).

claims.claim: Paired representation contrasts under a common executor, followed by a changed admission rule applied to unchanged programs; estimates evaluator-policy dependence under the tested contract, not model rankings and not a general causal capability effect.

anchors: Sec. 4.6, p.8 and Table 6, p.8: ACEBench model rankings before vs after removing validated flawed tasks; 18/30 models shift (App. E, p.20)
Sec. 4.6, p.8: random-removal null baseline over 100 trials - Kendall's tau 0.871 (cleaned) vs 0.960 (random, 95% CI 0.935-0.981); pairwise flip rate 5.75% vs 1.50% (95% CI 0.46-2.65)
Sec. 4.6, p.8: 'Table 6 is based on a single evaluation run per model due to computational cost'
Sec. 2.2 / Table 7, p.14: 'Too lenient' - a trivial do-nothing model succeeds on 38% of tau-bench tasks (p.3, p.13), an evaluation rule admitting wrong artifacts
agentsuite_overlap.summary: The general claim that an evaluation-side choice changes reported capability is already established by AgentSuite, with disciplined controls (null baseline, single-run caveat) and a much larger evidence base than ours (5086 tasks, 30 models, expert-validated F1 0.791-0.874).

anchors: Sec. 4.6, p.8: AgentSuite varies the TASK SET and re-runs models - a between-set comparison whose unit is (model, task) and whose output is a leaderboard
Sec. 3.1-3.3, pp.4-5: no execution and no per-artifact rule re-application, so an artifact-level counterfactual is not producible
Sec. 4.1-4.2, pp.5-6: unit of analysis is the task, not a submitted program
agentsuite_distinction.description: Ours holds the generated program bytes fixed and varies only the admission rule, paired at the instance level, with a preregistered +/-10pp equivalence margin for the representation contrasts and a 6.2%-47.7% rejection rate across arms. Program bytes are fixed between policy evaluations, not across representation arms. This is a within-artifact counterfactual, a genuinely different estimator - but a narrower claim than AgentSuite's (we claim nothing about model rankings).

claims.evidence_strength: high for overlap (anchored to Sec. 4.6/Table 6 and App. E); moderate for the distinction (comparison of estimators from paper text plus our manuscript's H1-R3 description)
claims.would_agentsuite_have_produced_same_find: No for the byte-fixed part (no execution, no per-artifact re-decision). But the asymmetry must be stated: if we had framed our result as 'removing flawed tasks changes reported capability / rankings', AgentSuite would have produced that finding first with stronger evidence. Our defensible framing is the narrow one we already use (unchanged programs, changed admission rule, no ranking claim).
claims.differentiating_evidence: The same adapted-COBA study; specifically the read-out question 'can a static, task-level audit produce a per-program admission counterfactual?' plus a counterfactual framing test (restate our headline as a task-removal ranking claim and check whether it is a replication of Sec. 4.6).
claims.limitations: We did not re-run AgentSuite's ACEBench analysis, so we cannot quantify the strength of the overlap, only establish it from the published numbers. Our own estimate is single-route, two task families, one margin, with the lower-level contrasts recorded as inconclusive (our own limitation statement, 11_limits.tex).

claims.claim: Independent cryptographic predicates and full fresh program replay against retained public inputs.

anchors: Sec. 3.2, p.4: Stage 1 is rule-based structural filtering only
Sec. 3.3, p.4-5: Stage 2 is taxonomy-guided LLM judgment; no execution of candidate programs and no predicate recomputation

App. A, p.12: 'Task-specific validation methods, such as unit-test augmentation in SWE-Bench or execution-based matching in SQL benchmarks, rely on deterministic semantics and executable environments, limiting their applicability beyond narrow domains' - execution is cited as related work they deliberately do not generalize
Sec. 4.5, p.8: BFCL V4 ground truths 'may additionally become stale as external information changes, highlighting a maintenance challenge' - a staleness observation with no replay mechanism
agentsuite_overlap.summary: Overlap is at the level of the shared goal (verifiable ground truth) only; mechanically there is none.

anchors: Sec. 3.1-3.3, pp.4-5: pipeline operates on static task artifacts with LLM judging; no execution module at any stage
App. A, p.12: execution-based validation treated as out-of-scope narrow-domain work
agentsuite_distinction.description: Ours introduces executable ground truth where the artifact is a program and the ground truth is a cryptographic relation, and replays admitted programs against retained public inputs (852/852 reference-replay agreement; staged full candidate re-executing 851 admitted programs), explicitly not fresh model generation.

claims.evidence_strength: high (direct absence confirmed over the full 20 pages; 'execution' occurs once, in App. A related work, p.12)
claims.would_agentsuite_have_produced_same_find: No. There is no execution stage; and their structural filter targets tool-call schemas, not program source semantics.
claims.differentiating_evidence: Not needed for the contrast with AgentSuite (already clear); the open question is against the wider execution-based-validation literature (SWE-Bench unit tests, SQL execution matching - the very works AgentSuite cites, p.12), which is outside this worker's scope.
claims.limitations: Do not claim to have invented execution-based verification; the novelty is its application to security attack programs with an independent cryptographic predicate and an explicit non-regeneration caveat. Our staged re-execution is a separate, staged candidate and is not part of the executed evidence base.

claims.claim: Complementarity of authenticated evidence and claim-specific joins in bounded adversarial attribution tests, using existing provenance mechanisms.

anchors: Full text pp.1-20: 'provenance' 0 hits, 'attribution' 0 hits, 'signature' (cryptographic) 0 hits, 'admission' 0 hits, 'replay' 0 hits, 'counterfactual' 0 hits; 'signed' occurs only as 'assigned'
Fig. 1, p.2 and Sec. 3.1, p.4: Ground Truth is a design-time reference trajectory, not runtime evidence
Sec. 3.4, p.5 and App. D.3, p.18: adversarial rebuttal reviews a flagged TASK judgment, not a claim-evidence binding
App. C.1-C.2, p.15: issue-guided repair edits benchmark artifacts, not execution evidence
agentsuite_overlap.summary: No overlap at the level of mechanism; overlap only at the level of the goal (reliable evaluation).

anchors: Sec. 3.1, p.4: the four-component model contains no runtime-evidence component
App. A, p.12: related work covers benchmark validity, agent benchmark validation, but not evidence binding for observed executions
agentsuite_distinction.description: Our artifact is a claim-specific attribution policy (observer-signed record over exact executed bytes and captured stdout; reference-signed recomputation of the task predicate from private target state; role authorization; digest agreement; replay policy; the claimant's own claims block excluded from the decision), validated by bounded mechanized testing (1407 mutants x 2 readings = 11256 evaluations, no observed soundness violation), live-target and loopback-ingress exercises against fabricated claims, and an in-toto inspection reproducing 21/22 decisions (22/22 with a shared replay ledger).

claims.evidence_strength: high for the absence (full-text term search over all 20 pages); moderate for the novelty, because the underlying mechanisms are pre-existing (in-toto, SLSA) - the novelty is the policy plus its test regime, not the machinery
claims.would_agentsuite_have_produced_same_find: No. Nothing in COBA's component model or pipeline touches runtime evidence, so this is the candidate with the least overlap with the comparator.
claims.differentiating_evidence: The adapted-COBA study should record whether ANY COBA taxonomy category corresponds to 'the evidence does not bind the claimed execution'. Separately, positioning against the provenance literature (in-toto, SLSA, ORTHRUS, PROV-AGENT - cited in our own related work) is required and was not audited here.
claims.limitations: Our six-release documentary audit (0/6 satisfy a nine-field rubric) is documentary, NOT external executable validation, and must not be presented as a benchmark-validation result that AgentSuite lacks. The in-toto agreement arm and the mutant-testing counts are recorded (not re-executed) in our current evidence base, per 11_limits.tex.

claims.claim: An integrated security-specific empirical method, rather than generic discovery that benchmark flaws distort performance.

anchors: Abstract, p.1: 'Our analysis shows that benchmark flaws are widespread and materially affect evaluation outcomes'
p.2: issues affect on average 27% of tasks
p.1 and Sec. 4.6, p.8: removing flawed tasks 'alters 60% of the model rankings in ACEBench' (18/30 models shift, App. E, p.20)
p.1 and Table 3, p.6: F1 0.791-0.874 against expert judgments across six benchmarks
Table 4, p.7: generalization to unseen benchmarks (BFCL V4, NexusBench)
App. A, p.12: AgentSuite already cites ABC as the design-level counterpart of this genre
agentsuite_overlap.summary: The generic half of C5 is AgentSuite's headline and its third stated contribution (p.1), established with stronger evidence than ours; it is not ours to claim.

anchors: Full text pp.1-20: 'security' 0 hits, 'attack' 0 hits, 'cryptograph' 0 hits
Sec. 2.1, p.2: audited benchmarks are tool-calling, conversational and function-calling agent benchmarks (BFCL V3, ACEBench, DrafterBench, tau-bench, tau^2-bench, CFB) - not attack programs
Sec. 3.1-3.3, pp.4-5: no execution, no evidence-binding (see C3, C4)
agentsuite_distinction.description: The security-attack instantiation (cryptographic attack programs, three-way stage separation, provenance-based attribution, six-release documentary audit) is not covered by AgentSuite. The increment for C5 is the integration in this domain, not the discovery that benchmark flaws matter.

claims.evidence_strength: high (the generic claim is directly and explicitly made by the comparator, with anchors on p.1, p.2, p.7, p.8)
claims.would_agentsuite_have_produced_same_find: Partly yes: for the generic claim ('benchmark flaws distort performance'), AgentSuite already has it with a larger sample and stronger validation. For the security-specific integration, no.
claims.differentiating_evidence: The adapted-COBA study, extended with a domain-transfer read-out: do COBA's component categories transfer to attack-program task cards, and do the residual failures that only our executable counterfactual exposes (admission rejections, attribution gaps) fall outside the taxonomy?
claims.limitations: C5 must be worded so that it does not restate the generic claim as new. ABC was assigned to a different worker and was not assessed here; cross-worker synthesis is root's.

summary.overall_verdict: The evidence does not support a general methodological contribution over AgentSuite. It supports a domain-specific instrument for security-agent attack evaluation whose mechanism differs from COBA in three places (byte-fixed admission counterfactual; independent cryptographic predicate with program replay; claim-specific attribution contract), while the general principle behind C1 and C5 is already established by AgentSuite and ABC.
summary.strongest_genuine_increment: The byte-fixed admission-policy counterfactual evaluated by an independent cryptographic predicate with full program replay (C2+C3): the only part of the paper a static, task-level, LLM-judged audit pipeline structurally cannot produce.
summary.strongest_overlap: The component-based separation-of-validity-sources template (C1: Table 2, p.3; Sec. 3.1 Eq. 1, p.4) and the generic 'flaws distort performance' empirical result (C5: pp.1-2, 7-8).
summary.single_most_important_open_differentiato: Whether an adapted COBA audit of our task cards can flag the same admission-policy and attribution defects - i.e. whether our increment is a new measurement modality (execution-based, artifact-level counterfactual plus evidence binding) or merely a domain transplant of AgentSuite's principle. Minimal design proposed in REPORT.md section 6; NOT launched.
